description: An introduction to work as force acting over a distance, the different forms and transformations of energy, the conservation of energy, and power as the rate of doing work, including renewable and non-renewable energy sources.

mcq.questionText: In physics, work is done when:

options.text: A force moves a body through a distance
A force is applied but nothing moves

mcq.explanation: Work is done only when a force moves an object through a distance in the direction of the force. Exam Tip: No movement, no work in physics - even if you feel tired holding a load still.

mcq.questionText: Work done is calculated using the formula:
mcq.explanation: Work = force x distance (in the direction of the force). Exam Tip: W = F x d. Multiply, do not divide.

mcq.questionText: The SI unit of work is the:
mcq.explanation: The SI unit of work is the joule (J), which equals one newton-metre. Exam Tip: 1 joule = 1 newton x 1 metre. Joule = work/energy; watt = power.

mcq.questionText: A force of 10 N moves a box a distance of 4 m. The work done is:
mcq.explanation: Work = force x distance = 10 x 4 = 40 J. Exam Tip: Multiply force by distance. Option 2.5 divides instead.
Energy is the capacity (ability) to do work. Exam Tip: Energy and work share the same unit, the joule.

mcq.questionText: The SI unit of energy is the:
mcq.explanation: The SI unit of energy is the joule (J). Exam Tip: Energy and work both use the joule. Power uses the watt.

mcq.questionText: Energy stored in a body because of its position or state is called:
mcq.explanation: Stored energy due to position is potential energy. Exam Tip: Potential = stored (raised stone, stretched spring). Kinetic = due to motion.

mcq.questionText: Energy possessed by a body because of its motion is called:
mcq.explanation: Energy due to movement is kinetic energy. Exam Tip: A moving car, flowing water and wind all have kinetic energy.
Power = work done / time taken, which is the rate of doing work. Exam Tip: Power measures how quickly energy is used or work is done.

mcq.questionText: The SI unit of power is the:
mcq.explanation: The SI unit of power is the watt (W), which equals one joule per second. Exam Tip: 1 watt = 1 joule per second. Watt = power; joule = energy.

mcq.questionText: If 200 J of work is done in 10 seconds, the power is:
mcq.explanation: Power = work / time = 200 / 10 = 20 W. Exam Tip: Divide work by time. Option 2000 multiplies instead.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
mcq.explanation: Solar (sunlight) energy is renewable, while coal, petrol and diesel are fossil fuels that run out. Exam Tip: Renewable: solar, wind, hydro, geothermal. Non-renewable: coal, oil, natural gas.

mcq.questionText: When a stone is thrown upwards, its kinetic energy changes into:
mcq.explanation: As the stone rises it slows down (loses kinetic energy) and gains height (gains potential energy). Exam Tip: Rising object: kinetic to potential. Falling object: potential to kinetic.

mcq.questionText: The law of conservation of energy states that energy can:

options.text: Neither be created nor destroyed, only changed from one form to another

mcq.explanation: Energy is never created or destroyed; it only changes from one form to another. Exam Tip: Total energy stays constant; it just transforms.

mcq.questionText: A crane lifts a load of 500 N through a height of 3 m. The work done against gravity is:
mcq.explanation: Work = force x distance = 500 x 3 = 1500 J. Exam Tip: Lifting work = weight x height. Force is the load's weight (500 N).

fib.questionText: Work is done when a force moves a body through a ____.
fib.explanation: Work requires the body to move through a distance in the direction of the force. Exam Tip: No distance moved, no work done, however large the force.

fib.questionText: Work done is calculated as work = force x ____.
fib.explanation: The formula for work is force multiplied by the distance moved. Exam Tip: W = F x d.

fib.questionText: The SI unit of work and energy is the ____.
fib.explanation: Both work and energy are measured in joules because they are the same type of quantity. Exam Tip: 1 joule = 1 newton-metre.

fib.questionText: Energy is defined as the ability to do ____.
fib.explanation: Energy is the capacity to do work, which is why the two share a unit. Exam Tip: This is why energy and work share the joule.

fib.questionText: Energy possessed by a body due to its motion is called ____ energy.
fib.explanation: Energy due to movement is kinetic energy. Exam Tip: Kinetic = moving; potential = stored.

fib.questionText: Energy stored in a body due to its position is called ____ energy.
fib.explanation: Stored energy due to position or state is potential energy. Exam Tip: A raised object or stretched spring has potential energy.

fib.questionText: Power is the rate of doing work, calculated as power = work / ____.
fib.explanation: Power is work divided by the time taken to do it. Exam Tip: P = W / t. Its unit is the watt (J/s).

fib.questionText: The SI unit of power is the ____.
fib.explanation: Power is measured in watts, one watt being one joule per second. Exam Tip: 1 watt = 1 joule per second.

fib.questionText: The energy of moving water used to generate electricity in dams comes originally from the ____ (name one renewable source).
fib.explanation: The Sun drives the water cycle, so hydro energy is ultimately solar and renewable. Exam Tip: Hydro, wind and solar are renewable and ultimately linked to the Sun.

fib.questionText: The law of conservation of energy states that energy is neither created nor ____.
fib.explanation: Energy can only change form; it is never created or destroyed. Exam Tip: Energy only transforms; the total remains constant.

tf.questionText: Work is done only when a force moves a body through a distance.
tf.explanation: Work in physics requires movement through a distance in the direction of the force. Exam Tip: Holding a load still does NO work in physics.

tf.questionText: The SI unit of work is the newton.
tf.explanation: The unit of work is the joule; the newton is the unit of force. Exam Tip: Work = joule; force = newton. Do not swap them.

tf.questionText: Energy is the ability to do work.
tf.explanation: Energy is defined as the capacity to do work. Exam Tip: This link is why energy and work share the joule.

tf.questionText: A moving car has potential energy because of its motion.
tf.explanation: Energy due to motion is kinetic energy, not potential energy. Exam Tip: Motion = kinetic energy, not potential.

tf.questionText: Power is the rate of doing work.
tf.explanation: Power measures how fast work is done, equal to work divided by time. Exam Tip: Power = work / time; unit watt (J/s).

tf.questionText: The SI unit of power is the watt.
tf.explanation: Power is measured in watts, one joule per second. Exam Tip: Watt = power; joule = energy.

tf.questionText: Solar energy is a non-renewable source of energy.
tf.explanation: Solar energy is renewable because sunlight does not run out. Exam Tip: Solar is renewable; coal, oil and gas are non-renewable.

tf.questionText: When a body falls, its potential energy changes into kinetic energy.
tf.explanation: As a body falls it loses height (potential) and gains speed (kinetic). Exam Tip: Falling: potential to kinetic. Rising: kinetic to potential.

tf.questionText: Energy can be created from nothing.
tf.explanation: By the law of conservation of energy, energy cannot be created; it only changes form. Exam Tip: Energy only changes form; it cannot be made from nothing.

tf.questionText: Work and energy are measured in the same unit, the joule.
tf.explanation: Work and energy are the same type of quantity, so both use the joule. Exam Tip: Same quantity type, same unit (joule).

summary.correctAnswer: The product of a force and the distance moved in the direction of the force: work = force x distance.
summary.explanation: No work is done unless the body moves through a distance. Exam Tip: W = F x d; multiply, do not divide.

summary.correctAnswer: The SI unit of work and energy, equal to one newton-metre (the work done when a force of 1 N moves a body 1 m).
summary.explanation: Both work and energy are measured in joules. Exam Tip: Joule = work/energy; newton = force; watt = power.

summary.correctAnswer: The ability or capacity to do work, measured in joules.
summary.explanation: Energy exists in many forms such as kinetic, potential, heat, light and sound. Exam Tip: Energy and work share the same unit, the joule.

summary.correctAnswer: The energy possessed by a body because of its motion.
summary.explanation: A moving car, flowing water and wind all have kinetic energy. Exam Tip: Kinetic = moving; the faster it moves, the more kinetic energy.

summary.correctAnswer: The energy stored in a body because of its position or state.
summary.explanation: A raised stone or a stretched spring has potential energy. Exam Tip: Potential = stored; height or stretch gives potential energy.

summary.correctAnswer: The rate of doing work, calculated as power = work / time.
summary.explanation: Power tells you how quickly work is done or energy is used. Exam Tip: P = W / t; divide work by time.

summary.correctAnswer: The SI unit of power, equal to one joule per second.
summary.explanation: A machine using 1 J of energy each second has a power of 1 watt. Exam Tip: 1 watt = 1 joule per second; watt = power.

summary.correctAnswer: The law that energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only changed from one form to another.
summary.explanation: The total energy in a system stays constant while forms change. Exam Tip: Total energy is constant; it only transforms.

summary.correctAnswer: The change of energy from one form into another, such as potential energy changing into kinetic energy.
summary.explanation: A falling stone changes potential energy into kinetic energy. Exam Tip: Trace energy step by step; the total is conserved.

summary.correctAnswer: Renewable sources can be replaced naturally and do not run out (solar, wind, hydro), while non-renewable sources run out once used (coal, oil, natural gas).
summary.explanation: Renewable sources are cleaner and sustainable, unlike fossil fuels. Exam Tip: Renewable: solar, wind, hydro, geothermal. Non-renewable: coal, oil, gas.

hoq.questionText: A labourer lifts a sack weighing 250 N onto a lorry platform 2 m high in 5 seconds. Calculate the work done and the power developed.
hoq.explanation: Work = force x distance = 250 x 2 = 500 J, and power = work / time = 500 / 5 = 100 W. Exam Tip: Find WORK first (force x distance), then POWER (work / time). Do not multiply by time.

hoq.questionText: In a hydroelectric station, water stored high in a dam flows down and turns turbines that generate electricity, which lights a bulb (light and heat). Identify the MAIN energy changes in order.

options.text: Potential energy -> kinetic energy -> electrical energy -> light (and heat) energy

hoq.explanation: Water stored high has potential energy, flowing down it becomes kinetic, the turbines produce electrical energy, and the bulb gives light and heat. Exam Tip: Trace energy step by step; energy is conserved, only changing form.

hoq.questionText: Pump A does 6000 J of work in 30 s; Pump B does 6000 J in 20 s. Which is more powerful, and what are their powers?

options.text: Pump A: 200 W, Pump B: 300 W - Pump B is more powerful
Pump A: 300 W, Pump B: 200 W - Pump A is more powerful
Both have equal power of 6000 W
Pump A: 180000 W, Pump B: 120000 W

hoq.explanation: Pump A: 6000 / 30 = 200 W and Pump B: 6000 / 20 = 300 W, so Pump B does the same work in less time and is more powerful. Exam Tip: Same work in LESS time = MORE power.
